about: The expert council, item 7, part 1 (queue expert-council): people who matter. The best sales leaders and diplomats do not network; they keep a short list of people, stay in touch on a rhythm, and give before they ask. Most people let the ties that matter most fade by accident. This is that system for anyone: a few names, one small touch a day, never a database. Paraphrased from common practice; content only, the screen is not built yet. Names and notes stay on the person's device and are never synced without their choice.

loop.cue: One name a day on Today, chosen by the app: the person most overdue for their circle.
loop.smallestStep: Send one honest line (a ready opener below) or make a two-minute call, then tap Done.
loop.reward: The circle fills in as people are reached; a quiet count of ties kept warm this month.
loop.environment: The opener is ready to send through the share sheet; birthdays and anniversaries arrive from the calendar the person already has.
loop.review: Once a quarter, five minutes: who moved closer, who drifted, who should join or leave a circle.
loop.constraint: The list must stay short. More than about fifty names and the system dies.

circles.name: Inner circle
circles.who: The people you would call at 2 a.m., and who would call you.

circles.name: Close
circles.who: Family and friends whose lives you want to be part of.
circles.form: a call, a visit or a real message

circles.name: Mentors and sponsors
circles.who: People a step or two ahead who know your work.
circles.form: an update on what you did with their advice, then one question

circles.name: Peers and allies
circles.who: People in your field you learn with and would work with again.
circles.form: something useful to them: an article, an introduction, a thank-you

circles.name: Dormant ties
circles.who: Good people you have lost touch with: old colleagues, teachers, classmates.
circles.form: a short note with no ask

changes: last touch (set by the Done tap)
one line to remember (their child's exam, a surgery, a new job)
never: anything they told you in confidence
health or money details of another person
a score or rating of a person

openers.text: I thought of you today because of {reason}. No need to reply; I hope you are well.
I used what you told me about {topic}, and it worked: {result}. Thank you.
This made me think of your work on {topic}: {link}. The part on {point} seemed useful.
I saw the news about {event}. Well deserved; I am glad for you.
I heard about {event}. I am here. Shall I call tonight, or would tomorrow be easier?
You and {name} are working on the same problem from two sides. Would you both like an introduction?

giveFirst: Introduce two people who should know each other (ask both first).
Pass on a job, a client or a piece of praise in front of others.
Share something you learned the hard way.
Show up: the function, the hospital, the difficult day.
Remember the thing they were worried about, and ask how it went.

asking.say: When you do need help, a good ask is small, specific and easy to refuse.
asking.shape: What I am trying to do: ... | The one thing I am asking: ... | Why I thought of you: ... | It is fine to say no.
asking.rule: Never the first message after years of silence. Warm the tie first, with no ask.

moments.do: A call beats a message; a message beats a group post.
Go or call within a week, and again after a month, when everyone else has stopped.
Offer one useful thing for the new role.
A personal line to the inner and close circles, not a forward.

safety: A message asking for money, a code or secrecy from someone on your list is checked by calling them back on the number you already have.
Agree a family code word for calls that claim an emergency (see queue family-security-programme).

persona.who: A busy manager who has moved cities

persona.starts: inner and close: one call a day
mentors: three names, one update a quarter
